title: THE GOVERNANCE OF INSTITUTIONAL SILENCE: When Organizations Know the Truth but Their Governance Systems Fail to Respond
summary: Examines what happens after a concern has been reported: how governance systems that receive, filter, escalate and respond to information can fail to turn it into accountable action. Identifies five mechanisms of structural silence, draws on Marchand v. Barnhill as a documented legal example, and proposes the Institutional Silence Risk Framework (ISRF), a five-dimension diagnostic assessed on its weakest dimension. Presented as a conceptual framework; its dimensions, indicators and rating method have not been empirically validated.

title: BEYOND COMPLIANCE: THE ARCHITECTURE OF ETHICAL INSTITUTIONAL CONDUCT
summary: Connects regulatory conformity, ethical leadership, risk management and institutional accountability into one integrated governance perspective. Examines how organizations demonstrate genuine integrity through decisions, behaviour and measurable results, rather than only explaining the rules.

title: The Governance of Institutional Memory: Institutional Knowledge, Decision Continuity, and the Prevention of Governance Failure
summary: Proposes an integrated Institutional Memory Governance (IMG) framework addressing how institutions can preserve their capacity to learn, make informed decisions, maintain continuity and remain accountable when leadership and personnel change. The research goes beyond conventional records management to examine how institutions preserve not only documents, but also the knowledge, context, rationale, experience and lessons behind institutional decisions. It introduces seven interconnected governance dimensions and an initial assessment model, the Institutional Memory Maturity Index (IMMI), with particular relevance to public administration and state-building. Presented as a conceptual and applied governance framework; the proposed model and index require further expert review, empirical validation and field testing.

title: From Governance Accountability Architecture to Governance Legitimacy — EGIA™ Part 42
summary: A published installment examining why assigned responsibilities, documented decision processes and effective controls do not by themselves establish legitimate grounds for recognizing and accepting governance authority and decisions.

title: From Governance Robustness to Governance Assurance Architecture — EGIA™ Part 40
summary: A published installment examining how governance robustness is translated into a structured governance assurance architecture.

title: From Governance Assurance Architecture to Governance Accountability Architecture — EGIA™ Part 41
summary: A published installment examining the transition from governance assurance architecture to governance accountability architecture, emphasizing accountability for governance decisions and outcomes.

title: A National Project to Unify the General Framework for Governance and Risk Management in Lebanon
summary: A national-level working paper proposing a unified general framework for governance and risk management in Lebanon.

title: Ethical Voice in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: When AI Participates in Decision-Making, Who Has the Right to Disagree?
summary: Research examining ethical voice, disagreement and accountability when artificial intelligence participates in decision-making.

summary: Research on the psychological and behavioral dimensions of governance.

summary: A published installment in the EGIA™ series, addressing governance learning and adaptation.

title: Unified Behavioral-Structural Governance Theory
summary: Research connecting behavioral and structural dimensions of governance.

title: EGIA Core Framework
summary: Core framework publication of the EGIA™ series.

title: FinTech Governance Intelligence™
summary: Research on governance intelligence in FinTech.

title: Enterprise Governance Intelligence Architecture (EGIA): A Sector Application Paper — FinTech Governance Integration
summary: A sector-application companion to the EGIA Core Framework, applying the architecture conceptually to FinTech environments through six intelligence domains: Strategic Performance, Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Control, AI Governance and Decision Intelligence. A conceptual, design-science paper without empirical validation, intended to invite structured critique and pilot testing.

title: FROM CRIME ECONOMY TO STATE INTEGRITY: Anti-Narcotics and Anti-Money Laundering as Foundations for Modern State-Building in Lebanon
summary: Research examining the links between drug trafficking, money laundering, illicit finance, corruption and state integrity in Lebanon. It proposes an integrated governance approach focused on financial intelligence, asset tracing, enforcement, recovery, institutional accountability and state resilience.

title: Digital Ownership by Design: Native Digital Assets, Tokenization, Digital Rights, Financial Transformation and Governance through EGIA™
summary: A conceptual, professional and policy-oriented study of ownership in tokenized and digitally native assets, arguing that technical control does not automatically constitute legal ownership. It proposes a Digital Ownership Maturity Model, readiness gates and a token lifecycle framework, and applies EGIA™ as a governance architecture. It does not constitute legal, financial, investment, tax or regulatory advice, and EGIA™ is not presented as an international standard or certification scheme.

title: Insurance Sales Excellence Framework™
summary: A behavioral and governance-based approach to insurance advisory practice, developed within the Governance Psychology™ research domain. It repositions insurance professionals as Behavioral Risk Advisors and introduces the Three Questions Model™, a structured diagnostic for identifying protection gaps. Developed in the Lebanese insurance market and offered as a transferable conceptual model.

title: From Governance Resilience to Governance Robustness and Stress Testing — EGIA™ Part 39
summary: A published installment in the EGIA™ series, addressing governance robustness and stress testing.
